EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ with sudden onset severe headache and
vomiting. Rule out subarachnoid hemorrhage.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast CT of the head was performed. Axial images
were obtained from the skull base to the vertex.

COMPARISON: None.

FINDINGS:

There is hyperdensity within the basal cisterns and sulci of the
bilateral cerebral convexities, consistent with subarachnoid
hemorrhage. No intraparenchymal hemorrhage is identified. No
hydrocephalus. Mild cerebral edema is noted. No midline shift.
The osseous structures are intact. No fracture identified.
Visualized paranasal sinuses are clear.

IMPRESSION:

1. Subarachnoid hemorrhage involving the basal cisterns and
   bilateral cerebral convexities.
2. Mild cerebral edema without hydrocephalus or midline shift.
3. Recommend urgent neurosurgical consultation.

FINAL REPORT

EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ with history of hypertension presenting
with acute onset right-sided weakness and aphasia.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast CT of the head was performed. Axial images
were obtained from the skull base to the vertex.

COMPARISON: No prior imaging available.

FINDINGS:

There is a hyperdense lesion in the left basal ganglia measuring
approximately 3.2 x 2.8 cm, consistent with acute hypertensive
intraparenchymal hemorrhage. There is surrounding vasogenic edema
with mild mass effect on the left lateral ventricle. Midline shift
of approximately 4 mm to the right is noted. No hydrocephalus.
No herniation. Osseous structures intact.

IMPRESSION:

1. Acute left basal ganglia hypertensive intraparenchymal hemorrhage
   measuring 3.2 x 2.8 cm.
2. Mild mass effect with 4 mm rightward midline shift.
3. Surrounding vasogenic edema.
4. Neurosurgical consultation recommended.

FINAL REPORT

EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ with altered mental status and fever.
History of ___ immunocompromised state.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast CT of the head was performed. Axial images
were obtained from the skull base to the vertex.

COMPARISON: CT head ___.

FINDINGS:

There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect. No midline
shift. The ventricles are mildly enlarged, likely reflecting mild
cerebral atrophy. There are multiple hypodense lesions in the right
frontal and parietal lobes with surrounding edema, the largest
measuring approximately 1.5 cm. Findings are concerning for
infectious or metastatic etiology. No herniation identified.
Osseous structures intact. Paranasal sinuses unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

1. Multiple hypodense lesions in the right frontal and parietal
   lobes with surrounding edema, concerning for infectious
   (abscess) or metastatic disease.
2. Mild cerebral atrophy.
3. MRI brain with and without contrast recommended for further
   characterization.

FINAL REPORT

EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W AND W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ with known history of glioblastoma
multiforme, status post resection and chemoradiation. Follow-up
imaging.

TECHNIQUE: CT of the head was performed before and after the
administration of intravenous contrast.

COMPARISON: MRI brain ___.

FINDINGS:

Post-surgical changes are noted in the right temporal lobe with
encephalomalacic changes at the resection site. There is an
irregular area of peripheral rim enhancement at the resection
margin measuring 3.8 x 3.1 cm, increased from prior. Moderate
surrounding vasogenic edema with effacement of the right lateral
ventricle. Midline shift of 6 mm to the left. No new hemorrhage.
Osseous structures intact.

IMPRESSION:

1. Interval increase in size of rim-enhancing lesion at the right
   temporal resection site, measuring 3.8 x 3.1 cm, concerning for
   tumor recurrence versus treatment-related changes.
2. Moderate surrounding vasogenic edema with 6 mm leftward midline
   shift.
3. MRI brain with perfusion sequences recommended for further
   evaluation.

FINAL REPORT

EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ involved in motor vehicle accident.
Loss of consciousness at scene. Rule out intracranial injury.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast CT of the head was performed. Axial images
were obtained from the skull base to the vertex. Bone algorithm
reconstructions obtained.

COMPARISON: None.

FINDINGS:

There is a small epidural hematoma along the right temporal convexity
measuring up to 8 mm in maximum thickness with associated right
temporal bone fracture extending through the squamosal portion.
There is no significant midline shift. No subdural hematoma. No
subarachnoid hemorrhage. No intraparenchymal contusion identified.
The ventricles are normal in size. The basal cisterns are patent.

IMPRESSION:

1. Small right temporal epidural hematoma measuring up to 8 mm
   associated with right temporal bone fracture.
2. No significant midline shift.
3. Urgent neurosurgical evaluation recommended.

EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ with progressive headache and blurred
vision over several weeks.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast CT of the head was performed. Axial images
were obtained from the skull base to the vertex.

COMPARISON: No prior CT available.

FINDINGS:

There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage. No midline shift or
herniation. The ventricles are mildly enlarged with periventricular
hypodensity suggestive of transependymal CSF flow, consistent with
communicating hydrocephalus. The basal cisterns appear effaced.
Sulci are diminished bilaterally. No focal parenchymal lesion
identified. Osseous structures intact.

IMPRESSION:

1. Communicating hydrocephalus with transependymal CSF flow and
   effacement of basal cisterns.
2. No acute hemorrhage.
3. Neurology and neurosurgery consultation recommended. LP
   consideration per clinical team.

FINAL REPORT

EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ with history of atrial fibrillation on
anticoagulation presenting with acute confusion and left-sided
facial droop.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast CT of the head was performed. Axial images
were obtained from the skull base to the vertex.

COMPARISON: CT head ___.

FINDINGS:

There is subtle hypodensity in the right MCA territory involving
the right insular cortex and right basal ganglia, consistent with
early acute ischemic infarction. No hemorrhagic transformation.
No mass effect or midline shift. The left hemisphere appears
unremarkable. The posterior fossa structures are intact. Osseous
structures intact. Paranasal sinuses clear.

IMPRESSION:

1. Early acute right MCA territory ischemic infarction involving
   the right insular cortex and right basal ganglia.
2. No hemorrhagic transformation.
3. Recommend urgent MRI brain with DWI for confirmation and extent
   delineation. Stroke team notification.

FINAL REPORT

EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ with history of chronic alcohol use
presenting with fall and head trauma. Rule out intracranial injury.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast CT of the head was performed. Axial images
were obtained from the skull base to the vertex.

COMPARISON: None.

FINDINGS:

There is a thin crescentic hyperdense extra-axial collection along
the right cerebral convexity consistent with acute subdural hematoma,
measuring up to 5 mm in maximum thickness. No significant mass effect
or midline shift. Bilateral frontal and temporal cerebral atrophy
is noted, consistent with chronic alcohol-related changes. No
intraparenchymal hemorrhage. Ventricles mildly enlarged. Osseous
structures intact without fracture.

IMPRESSION:

1. Acute right subdural hematoma measuring up to 5 mm without
   significant mass effect or midline shift.
2. Diffuse cerebral atrophy, likely related to chronic alcohol use.
3. Neurosurgical consultation recommended.

FINAL REPORT

EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ with history of hypertension and
diabetes presenting with dizziness and diplopia.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast CT of the head was performed. Axial images
were obtained from the skull base to the vertex.

COMPARISON: CT head ___.

FINDINGS:

There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage or territorial infarction.
No mass effect or midline shift. Moderate periventricular and
subcortical white matter hypodensities are present, increased compared
to prior examination, consistent with progressive chronic small vessel
ischemic disease. The posterior fossa structures appear intact. The
ventricles are mildly enlarged. Mild generalized cerebral atrophy.
No acute bony abnormality.

IMPRESSION:

1. No acute intracranial hemorrhage or large territorial infarction.
2. Progressive chronic small vessel ischemic disease compared to
   prior CT.
3. Mild generalized cerebral atrophy.
4. MRI brain recommended for further evaluation of posterior fossa
   structures and small acute infarcts.

FINAL REPORT

EXAMINATION: CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION: ___ year old ___ with new onset seizure. No prior
neurological history.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast CT of the head was performed. Axial images
were obtained from the skull base to the vertex.

COMPARISON: None available.

FINDINGS:

There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or midline
shift. No territorial infarction. The ventricles and sulci are
normal in size and configuration for the patient's stated age.
The basal cisterns are patent. No extra-axial fluid collections.
No focal parenchymal lesion identified. Osseous structures intact.
Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.

IMPRESSION:

1. No acute intracranial abnormality identified on non-contrast CT.
2. MRI brain with and without contrast recommended for more
   sensitive evaluation of seizure etiology including cortical
   dysplasia, low-grade tumor, or mesial temporal sclerosis.
